# Part B: Wheat in Jendouba {#sec-wheat}

Part B repeats the same steps for a winter cereal. The differences are
explained where they appear: the crop map is a **raster** instead of
polygons, the AOI is taken from that raster, and the crop parameters
come from a built-in FAO profile.

## Step 1: Define the inputs

```{r}
#| label: wheat-config

# The "Setting up" chunks (packages and helper functions) must run first
stopifnot("Run the chunks in 'Setting up' first (packages and helper functions)" =
            exists("check") && exists("plot_kc_months") && exists("plot_map"))

cereal_mask_path   <- "data/wheat/Season5_2023_2024_cereal_mask.tif"  # cereal map, 2023/24 season
wheat_class_code   <- 1L                              # value of wheat pixels in the map
wheat_period       <- c("2023-11-01", "2024-05-31")   # sowing to harvest
wheat_l3_region    <- "JEN"                           # WaPOR L3 region: Jendouba
wheat_download_dir <- "wapor_data/wheat"
wheat_output_dir   <- "outputs/Wheat_Winter2023_2024"
wheat_aoi_path     <- file.path(wheat_download_dir, "wheat_aoi.geojson")  # created in Step 2

dir.create(wheat_download_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
check(file.exists(cereal_mask_path), paste("cereal map found:", cereal_mask_path))
wheat_days <- as.integer(diff(as.Date(wheat_period))) + 1L
cat("Season length:", wheat_days, "days\n")
```

## Step 2: Look at the cereal map and create the AOI

```{r}
#| label: wheat-explore-inputs

cereal_mask_raw <- terra::rast(cereal_mask_path)
cereal_mask_raw

# Which values does the map contain, and how many pixels of each?
terra::freq(cereal_mask_raw)
```

::: callout-tip
## Checkpoint

Check that `wheat_class_code` in Step 1 matches the value of wheat in
the legend of your crop map. This map has a single value, 1 (cereal),
which we treat as wheat. It is 20 m in UTM zone 32N.
:::

There is no separate outline file for this study, so we use the
**outline of the cereal map** as the AOI and save it as a file:

```{r}
#| label: wheat-derive-aoi

wheat_aoi <- terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(cereal_mask_raw), crs = terra::crs(cereal_mask_raw)) |>
  sf::st_as_sf() |>
  sf::st_transform(4326)
sf::st_write(wheat_aoi, wheat_aoi_path, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

cereal_ha <- terra::freq(cereal_mask_raw)$count[1] * prod(terra::res(cereal_mask_raw)) / 10000
data.frame(
  aoi_area_ha    = round(as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_transform(wheat_aoi, 32632))) / 10000),
  cereal_area_ha = round(cereal_ha)
)
check(file.exists(wheat_aoi_path), paste("AOI saved:", wheat_aoi_path))
```

```{r}
#| label: wheat-leaflet-inputs
#| fig-cap: "The AOI (white) and the cereal map (orange)"

# The map shows the cereal mask at its full 20 m resolution

leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |>
  addRasterImage(cereal_mask_raw, colors = "#f4a300", opacity = 0.7, method = "ngb",
                 maxBytes = 64 * 1024^2) |>
  addPolygons(data = wheat_aoi, fill = FALSE, color = "white", weight = 2) |>
  addLegend(colors = c("#f4a300", "white"), labels = c("Cereal", "AOI"), position = "bottomright")
```

## Step 3: Crop parameters for wheat

For wheat we can start from the built-in FAO-56 profile and change
only what we know locally. To see all built-in crops, run
`wapor_list_crops()`. Besides the Kc values, wheat needs the four yield
factors explained at the end of this step (HI, AOT, fc, MC).

```{r}
#| label: wheat-crop-params

wheat_params <- wapor_custom_crop(
  base_crop   = "Winter Wheat",     # FAO-56 profile
  class_value = wheat_class_code,
  crop_name   = "Irrigated Winter Wheat",
  kc_ini      = 0.35,
  kc_mid      = 1.15,
  kc_end      = 0.30,
  HI          = 0.43,               # harvest index: share of above-ground biomass harvested as grain
  AOT         = 0.75,               # above-ground over total biomass ratio
  fc          = 1.0,                # light use efficiency correction factor (1 for C3 crops such as wheat)
  MC          = 0.15                # moisture content of the harvested grain
)
wheat_params
```

```{r}
#| label: wheat-kc-curve
#| fig-cap: "Daily Kc for winter wheat over the season"

wheat_l_dev <- wheat_days - (wheat_params$l_ini_days + wheat_params$l_mid_days + wheat_params$l_late_days)

wheat_kc_daily <- wapor_build_kc(
  kc_ini = wheat_params$kc_ini, kc_mid = wheat_params$kc_mid, kc_end = wheat_params$kc_end,
  l_ini  = wheat_params$l_ini_days, l_dev = wheat_l_dev,
  l_mid  = wheat_params$l_mid_days, l_late = wheat_params$l_late_days
)

plot_kc_months(wheat_kc_daily, wheat_period[1],
               c(wheat_params$l_ini_days, wheat_l_dev, wheat_params$l_mid_days, wheat_params$l_late_days),
               c("Initial (sowing, emergence)", "Development (tillering)",
                 "Mid-season (heading, grain filling)", "Late season (ripening)"),
               "Winter wheat Kc curve, November 2023 to May 2024")

check(length(wheat_kc_daily) == wheat_days, paste("Kc curve has", length(wheat_kc_daily), "daily values"))
check(wheat_l_dev > 0, paste("development stage:", wheat_l_dev, "days"))
```

::: callout-note
## Concept: why the wheat curve looks so different

Wheat is an annual crop: the field is almost bare after sowing (low
Kc), the canopy closes in late winter (high Kc) and the crop dries out
before harvest (low Kc again). The evergreen citrus canopy in Part A
keeps a nearly constant Kc all year.
:::

### The yield equation and the wheat factors

WaPOR does not measure yield directly. It measures **NPP**, the carbon
the crop fixed. The yield equation turns the seasonal NPP into total
biomass and then into harvestable grain:

![Yield estimation equation for wheat, and the meaning of each
factor.](images/wheat_yield_equation.png){width="100%"}

$$
TBP = \frac{NPP \times 22.222}{1000}
$$

$$
Y = HI \times AOT \times fc \times \frac{TBP}{1 - MC}
$$

| Term | Meaning | Wheat value |
|------------------|------------------------------------|------------------|
| NPP | Net primary production over the season, from WaPOR (gC/m²) | from WaPOR |
| TBP | Total biomass production (t DM/ha); 22.222 converts gC/m² to kg DM/ha, / 1000 gives t/ha | calculated |
| fc | Light use efficiency correction factor; 1 for C3 crops such as wheat (no correction) | 1.0 |
| AOT | Above-ground over total biomass ratio: 75% of the biomass is above ground (stems, leaves, ears) | 0.75 |
| HI | Harvest index: share of the above-ground biomass harvested as grain | 0.43 |
| MC | Moisture content of the harvested grain; dividing by (1 - MC) gives yield as harvested (fresh) weight | 0.15 |
| Y | Harvestable yield (t/ha) | calculated |

The next cell prints the factors stored in `wheat_params` and confirms
they are the values in the figure, so the yields in Step 8 use exactly
these factors.

```{r}
#| label: wheat-yield-factors

yield_factors <- data.frame(
  factor  = c("HI", "AOT", "fc", "MC"),
  meaning = c("harvest index", "above-ground over total biomass",
              "light use efficiency correction (C3)", "moisture content of grain"),
  value   = c(wheat_params$HI, wheat_params$AOT, wheat_params$fc, wheat_params$MC)
)
yield_factors

check(isTRUE(all.equal(yield_factors$value, c(0.43, 0.75, 1.0, 0.15))),
      "wheat yield factors match the yield equation figure (HI 0.43, AOT 0.75, fc 1.0, MC 0.15)")

# One worked example: a pixel with 500 gC/m2 of seasonal NPP
npp_example <- 500
tbp_example <- npp_example * 22.222 / 1000
y_example   <- wheat_params$HI * wheat_params$AOT * wheat_params$fc * tbp_example / (1 - wheat_params$MC)
cat(sprintf("NPP %d gC/m2 -> TBP %.1f t DM/ha -> harvestable yield %.2f t/ha\n",
            npp_example, tbp_example, y_example))
```

## Step 4: First look: seasonal AETI map

```{r}
#| label: wheat-seasonal-aeti-map
#| fig-cap: "Seasonal AETI (mm) over the Jendouba AOI, November 2023 to May 2024"

# Use the saved map if it exists (next runs, or no internet)
saved_map <- list.files(file.path(wheat_download_dir, "L3-AETI-D_seasonal"), "seasonal.*[.]tif$",
                        full.names = TRUE)
wheat_aeti_seasonal_path <- if (length(saved_map) > 0) saved_map[1] else wapor_map(
  region    = wheat_aoi_path,       # the AOI outline, not the crop map
  variable  = "L3-AETI-D",
  l3_region = wheat_l3_region,
  period    = wheat_period,
  folder    = wheat_download_dir,
  seasonal  = TRUE,
  mask      = TRUE
)

wheat_aeti_r <- terra::rast(wheat_aeti_seasonal_path)
plot_map(wheat_aeti_r, "Jendouba: seasonal AETI", "mm")

raster_stats(`Seasonal AETI (mm)` = wheat_aeti_r)
```

::: callout-tip
## Checkpoint

This map covers the whole AOI, not only wheat: forests and permanent
crops appear with higher AETI, bare and urban land with lower values.
Winter cereals in northern Tunisia typically consume 250 to 450 mm over
the season.
:::

## Step 5: Put the crop mask on the WaPOR grid

::: callout-note
## Concept: matching a crop map to the WaPOR grid

A crop map made by another project has its own grid, and it has to be
put on the WaPOR grid before the analysis. We do it in a way that works
for any pair of grids:

1.  set wheat = 1 and everything else = 0,
2.  average these values inside each WaPOR pixel, which gives the
    **wheat fraction** of that pixel (0 to 1),
3.  keep the WaPOR pixels that are **at least 50% wheat**
    (`wheat_min_fraction`).

In Jendouba the cereal map and the WaPOR data share exactly the same
20 m grid, so every fraction is 0 or 1 and every cereal pixel is kept.
:::

```{r}
#| label: wheat-isolate-mask
#| fig-cap: "Wheat crop mask on the WaPOR grid"

wheat_min_fraction <- 0.5

# 1 = wheat, 0 = anything else
wheat_binary <- terra::ifel(!is.na(cereal_mask_raw) & cereal_mask_raw == wheat_class_code, 1, 0)

# Wheat fraction of each WaPOR pixel
wheat_fraction <- terra::project(wheat_binary, wheat_aeti_r, method = "average")

wheat_mask <- terra::ifel(wheat_fraction >= wheat_min_fraction, wheat_class_code, NA)
names(wheat_mask) <- "crop_mask"

terra::plot(wheat_mask, col = "#f4a300", legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE, main = "Wheat crop mask",
            maxcell = terra::ncell(wheat_mask))
```

```{r}
#| label: wheat-mask-check

cereal_pixels <- terra::freq(cereal_mask_raw)$count[1]
kept_pixels   <- terra::global(!is.na(wheat_mask), "sum")[1, 1]
data.frame(cereal_pixels_in_map = cereal_pixels, wapor_pixels_kept = kept_pixels)
check(abs(kept_pixels / cereal_pixels - 1) < 0.01, "the mask keeps all cereal pixels (same grid)")
```

## Step 6: Download the data and run the seasonal analysis

The method is the same as for citrus (Part A, Step 6), with one addition:
for wheat we also estimate biomass, yield and water productivity from NPP
(@sec-yield), so NPP is downloaded as well.

### Download the WaPOR data (once)

The season has 21 dekads. AETI, T and NPP (20 m) are cut to the AOI,
RET and precipitation (L1) to the area around it. The first run downloads
about 105 files; after that, and without internet, the saved files in
`wapor_data/wheat/dekadal/` are used.

```{r}
#| label: wheat-download

wheat_data_dir <- file.path(wheat_download_dir, "dekadal")
wheat_aoi_v    <- terra::vect(wheat_aoi)

wheat_downloads <- list(
  AETI = download_wapor("L3-AETI-D", wheat_aoi_v, wheat_period, wheat_data_dir, wheat_l3_region),
  T    = download_wapor("L3-T-D",    wheat_aoi_v, wheat_period, wheat_data_dir, wheat_l3_region),
  NPP  = download_wapor("L3-NPP-D",  wheat_aoi_v, wheat_period, wheat_data_dir, wheat_l3_region),
  RET  = download_wapor("L1-RET-D",  wheat_aoi_v, wheat_period, wheat_data_dir, mask = FALSE),
  PCP  = download_wapor("L1-PCP-D",  wheat_aoi_v, wheat_period, wheat_data_dir, mask = FALSE)
)

data.frame(variable = names(wheat_downloads),
           files    = lengths(wheat_downloads),
           size_mb  = round(sapply(wheat_downloads, function(f) sum(file.size(f))) / 1e6, 1))
check(all(lengths(wheat_downloads) == 21), "21 dekads saved for every variable")
```

### Run the analysis

```{r}
#| label: wheat-indicators

wheat_indicators <- c(
  citrus_indicators,                                                    # consumption, demand, water source
  "agg_npp", "agg_biomass_kg", "agg_biomass_t", "yield_npp", "cwp_bwp"  # production
)
```

Now we describe the analysis and run it.

```{r}
#| label: wheat-run-analysis

wheat_config <- list(
  period        = wheat_period,
  aeti_var      = "L3-AETI-D",
  t_var         = "L3-T-D",
  npp_var       = "L3-NPP-D",
  ret_var       = "L1-RET-D",
  precip_var    = "L1-PCP-D",
  data_source   = "local",          # read the files saved in the download step
  folder        = wheat_data_dir,
  use_crop_mask = TRUE,             # required: otherwise every AOI pixel counts as wheat
  area_weighted = TRUE,
  keep_intermediates = FALSE,       # saves disk space
  indicators    = wheat_indicators
)

wheat_season <- wapor_run_seasonal_analysis(
  config      = wheat_config,
  crop_params = wheat_params,
  rasters     = list(crop_mask = wheat_mask),
  aoi_region  = wheat_aoi_path
)
```

```{r}
#| label: wheat-run-check

n_dekads <- nrow(wheat_season$dekad_table)
check(n_dekads == 21, paste("dekads in the season:", n_dekads, "(7 months x 3)"))

wheat_season$mask_class_stats

coverage_min <- sapply(wheat_season$coverage, function(r) {
  terra::global(terra::mask(r, wheat_season$h_mask), "min", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
})
coverage_min
check(all(coverage_min >= 0.999), "every variable has data for every dekad on every wheat pixel")
```

## Step 7: Month by month check

```{r}
#| label: wheat-monthly
#| fig-cap: "Monthly water consumption, crop demand and rain over the wheat fields"
#| fig-height: 5.5

plot_monthly(wheat_season, "Wheat: month by month")
```

::: callout-tip
## Checkpoint: what the chart should show

-   AETI is low after sowing (November, December), rises as the crop
    grows and peaks in March and April, then falls as the crop ripens.
-   ETc follows the shape of the Kc curve from Step 3.
-   Rain falls mostly from November to March, so in the first months
    rain can cover most of the consumption.
:::

```{r}
#| label: wheat-monthly-check

m <- monthly_table(wheat_season)
aeti_m <- m[m$variable == "AETI (consumed)", ]
t_m    <- m[m$variable == "T (transpiration)", ]
check(all(t_m$mm <= aeti_m$mm + 1e-6), "monthly T is below AETI in every month")
peak <- format(aeti_m$month[which.max(aeti_m$mm)], "%B")
check(peak %in% c("March", "April"), paste("AETI peaks in", peak))
```

## Step 8: Indicators and maps

```{r}
#| label: wheat-out-aeti-etc
#| fig-cap: "Seasonal AETI and crop water demand (ETc) for wheat"

wheat_etc <- wheat_season$etc_by_class[[as.character(wheat_class_code)]]$etc_seasonal

two_maps(wheat_season$seasonal_aeti$raster, "Seasonal AETI", "mm",
         wheat_etc, "Crop water demand (ETc)", "mm",
         palette1 = "YlGnBu", palette2 = "Oranges")

raster_stats(`AETI (mm)` = wheat_season$seasonal_aeti$raster,
             `T (mm)`    = wheat_season$seasonal_t$raster,
             `ETc (mm)`  = wheat_etc)
```

```{r}
#| label: wheat-out-adequacy-bf
#| fig-cap: "Adequacy and beneficial fraction for wheat"

two_maps(wheat_season$adequacy_etc, "Adequacy", "AETI / ETc",
         wheat_season$beneficial_fraction, "Beneficial fraction", "T / AETI",
         palette1 = "RdYlBu", palette2 = "YlGn", rev1 = FALSE, rev2 = TRUE)

raster_hist(wheat_season$adequacy_etc, "Adequacy (AETI / ETc)", ref = 1)

bf_max <- terra::global(wheat_season$beneficial_fraction, "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
check(bf_max <= 1 + 1e-6, sprintf("beneficial fraction never exceeds 1 (max = %.2f)", bf_max))
```

### Irrigation performance indicators

We now assess the wheat fields with the WaPOR-based irrigation
performance framework of Chukalla et al. (2022): **adequacy** (was the
crop water demand met?), **uniformity** (was water use even within a
field?) and **equity** (was water use even between fields?). The
equations and class limits are in @sec-indicators.

::: callout-note
## Concept: fields or blocks

Uniformity is calculated inside a field and equity between fields, so both
need field boundaries. Our crop map is a raster without field boundaries,
so we divide the area into regular **1 km blocks** (50 x 50 pixels of
20 m) and treat each block as a management unit. Blocks with fewer than
100 wheat pixels (4 ha) are left out. With a field or parcel map, use the
fields instead; the method is the same.
:::

**Adequacy classes.** Each wheat pixel is classed as poor, acceptable or
good; pixels above 1 consumed more than the crop demand.

```{r}
#| label: wheat-performance-adequacy
#| fig-cap: "Adequacy classes for wheat (Chukalla et al., 2022)"

adequacy_classes <- terra::classify(
  wheat_season$adequacy_etc,
  rcl = matrix(c(-Inf, 0.68, 1,
                 0.68, 0.80, 2,
                 0.80, 1.00, 3,
                 1.00,  Inf, 4), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE),
  right = TRUE                                   # classes include their upper limit
)
class_names <- c("Poor (A <= 0.68)", "Acceptable (0.68 to 0.8)", "Good (0.8 to 1)", "Above demand (A > 1)")
levels(adequacy_classes) <- data.frame(value = 1:4, class = class_names)

terra::plot(adequacy_classes, col = c("#d7191c", "#fdae61", "#1a9641", "#2c7bb6"), axes = FALSE,
            main = "Wheat adequacy classes", maxcell = terra::ncell(adequacy_classes))

adequacy_share <- terra::freq(adequacy_classes)
adequacy_share$area_ha  <- round(adequacy_share$count * prod(terra::res(adequacy_classes)) / 10000)
adequacy_share$share_pc <- round(100 * adequacy_share$count / sum(adequacy_share$count), 1)
adequacy_share[, c("value", "area_ha", "share_pc")]
```

::: callout-tip
## Checkpoint

The shares add up to 100%. Low adequacy over large areas is expected
where cereals get little or no irrigation in spring: the demand (ETc) is
calculated for a crop that never lacks water, so rain-fed or deficit
irrigated fields fall in the poor class. Check the pattern with the
irrigation schedule of the scheme before calling it water stress.
:::

**Uniformity and equity.** For each 1 km block we calculate the mean and
the standard deviation of seasonal AETI over its wheat pixels.

$$
Uniformity = 1 - \frac{sd(AETI)}{mean(AETI)} \qquad
Equity = CV = \frac{sd(\text{block means})}{mean(\text{block means})}
$$

```{r}
#| label: wheat-performance-uniformity
#| fig-cap: "Uniformity of water use within 1 km blocks of wheat"

aeti_w     <- wheat_season$seasonal_aeti$raster
block_fact <- 50                                          # 50 x 50 pixels of 20 m = 1 km
block_mean <- terra::aggregate(aeti_w, fact = block_fact, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
block_sd   <- terra::aggregate(aeti_w, fact = block_fact, fun = "sd", na.rm = TRUE)
block_n    <- terra::aggregate(!is.na(aeti_w), fact = block_fact, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)
use_block  <- block_n >= 100                              # at least 4 ha of wheat

uniformity <- terra::ifel(use_block, 100 * (1 - block_sd / block_mean), NA)
plot_map(uniformity, "Uniformity within 1 km blocks", "%", palette = "RdYlGn", rev = FALSE)

block_means <- terra::values(terra::ifel(use_block, block_mean, NA), na.rm = TRUE)[, 1]
equity_cv   <- 100 * sd(block_means) / mean(block_means)
equity_class <- cut(equity_cv, c(0, 10, 25, Inf), labels = c("good", "fair", "poor"))

data.frame(
  blocks_used         = length(block_means),
  mean_uniformity_pc  = round(terra::global(uniformity, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 1),
  min_uniformity_pc   = round(terra::global(uniformity, "min", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 1),
  equity_cv_pc        = round(equity_cv, 1),
  equity_class        = equity_class
)
```

::: callout-tip
## Checkpoint

Uniformity is between 0 and 100%. Compare it with the standard for the
irrigation method used in the blocks (drip 85%, sprinkler 75%, furrow
65%); blocks below the standard are where water use inside the fields is
uneven. An equity CV below 10% means water use is shared evenly between
blocks.
:::

**Climate normalization.** Part of the difference in water use between
blocks comes from the weather, not from management: a block with a higher
reference ET (RET) consumes more water under the same management.
Chukalla et al. (2022) remove this effect with a normalization factor:

$$
f_{norm} = \frac{\overline{RET}}{RET_i}
$$

where $\overline{RET}$ is the mean seasonal RET over the area and $RET_i$
the seasonal RET of pixel (or field) $i$. Multiplying AETI or water
productivity by $f_{norm}$ makes them comparable across the area.

```{r}
#| label: wheat-performance-normalization

ret_w  <- wheat_season$seasonal_ret$raster
f_norm <- terra::mask(terra::global(ret_w, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1] / ret_w, aeti_w)
raster_stats(`Climate normalization factor` = f_norm)
```

::: callout-tip
## Checkpoint

A factor close to 1 everywhere means the weather is similar over the whole
area, so differences in AETI come mostly from management. Factors that
differ by more than about 10% mean the climate varies across the area,
and AETI or CWP should be normalized before comparing fields.
:::

Next, the water source of the consumed water:

```{r}
#| label: wheat-out-green-blue
#| fig-cap: "Green (rain) and blue (irrigation) water for wheat"

wheat_green <- wheat_season$green_water
wheat_blue  <- wheat_season$blue_water

two_maps(wheat_green, "Green water", "mm", wheat_blue, "Blue water", "mm",
         palette1 = "Greens", palette2 = "Blues")

plot_green_blue_monthly(wheat_season, "Wheat: where the water came from, month by month")

gap <- terra::global(abs(wheat_green + wheat_blue - wheat_season$seasonal_aeti$raster), "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
check(gap < 0.01, sprintf("green + blue = AETI on every pixel (largest difference %.4f mm)", gap))

wheat_shortcut <- seasonal_shortcut(wheat_season)
data.frame(
  method   = c("Month by month (correct)", "Seasonal totals (wrong)"),
  green_mm = c(mean_of(wheat_green), mean_of(wheat_shortcut$green)),
  blue_mm  = c(mean_of(wheat_blue),  mean_of(wheat_shortcut$blue))
)
```

::: callout-note
## Concept: why the two methods differ so much for wheat

Winter wheat grows during the rainy season, but the rain is not spread
evenly: December and January are wet while the crop still uses little
water, and in April the crop uses a lot while rain decreases. Split
month by month, April's shortfall shows up as blue water (irrigation or
water stored in the soil). Split on the season totals, the winter
surplus would hide it, and the fields would look almost fully
rain-fed.
:::

```{r}
#| label: wheat-out-productivity
#| fig-cap: "Seasonal biomass and estimated grain yield for wheat"

two_maps(wheat_season$seasonal_biomass_t, "Biomass", "t DM/ha",
         wheat_season$yield_raster, "Grain yield", "t/ha",
         palette1 = "YlGn", palette2 = "YlOrBr")

raster_stats(`Biomass (t/ha)` = wheat_season$seasonal_biomass_t,
             `Yield (t/ha)`   = wheat_season$yield_raster)

data.frame(
  indicator = c("CWP, grain (kg/m³)", "BWP, dry biomass (kg/m³)"),
  value     = round(c(wheat_season$cwp, wheat_season$bwp), 2)
)

# Confirm the yield map follows the yield equation with the factors from Step 3
tbp       <- wheat_season$seasonal_biomass_t                       # TBP = NPP x 22.222 / 1000
y_formula <- wheat_params$HI * wheat_params$AOT * wheat_params$fc * tbp / (1 - wheat_params$MC)
y_gap     <- terra::global(abs(y_formula - wheat_season$yield_raster), "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
check(y_gap < 1e-6, sprintf("yield = HI x AOT x fc x TBP / (1 - MC) on every pixel (largest difference %.2g t/ha)", y_gap))
```

::: callout-tip
## Checkpoint

Wheat grain yields in northern Tunisia are typically 2 to 5 t/ha, and
crop water productivity for wheat is usually between 0.6 and 1.7 kg/m³.
For wheat, CWP is lower than BWP because grain is only part of the
biomass.
:::

# Results side by side {#sec-summary}

```{r}
#| label: summary-table

season_summary <- function(season, etc) {
  c(
    `Crop area (ha)`            = round(sum(season$mask_class_stats$area_ha, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `AETI (mm)`                 = mean_of(season$seasonal_aeti$raster),
    `Transpiration T (mm)`      = mean_of(season$seasonal_t$raster),
    `Crop demand ETc (mm)`      = mean_of(etc),
    `Rain (mm)`                 = mean_of(season$seasonal_pcp),
    `Effective rain (mm)`       = mean_of(season$seasonal_peff),
    `Green water (mm)`          = mean_of(season$green_water),
    `Blue water (mm)`           = mean_of(season$blue_water),
    `Adequacy (AETI / ETc)`     = mean_of(season$adequacy_etc),
    `Beneficial fraction`       = mean_of(season$beneficial_fraction),
    `Biomass (t DM/ha)`         = mean_of(season$seasonal_biomass_t),
    `Yield (t/ha)`              = mean_of(season$yield_raster),
    `CWP (kg/m³)`               = num_or_na(season$cwp),
    `BWP (kg/m³)`               = num_or_na(season$bwp)
  )
}

data.frame(
  indicator = names(season_summary(citrus_season, citrus_etc)),
  Citrus    = unname(season_summary(citrus_season, citrus_etc)),
  Wheat     = unname(season_summary(wheat_season, wheat_etc))
)
```

Citrus shows `NA` for biomass, yield, CWP and BWP on purpose: tree crop
yield comes from farm surveys, not from the NPP equation.

```{r}
#| label: crop-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Seasonal water balance per crop (mean over the crop mask)"

balance <- data.frame(
  crop   = rep(c("Citrus", "Wheat"), each = 2),
  source = rep(c("Green (rain)", "Blue (irrigation)"), times = 2),
  mm     = c(mean_of(citrus_green), mean_of(citrus_blue), mean_of(wheat_green), mean_of(wheat_blue))
)

ggplot(balance, aes(crop, mm, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Green (rain)" = "#43a047", "Blue (irrigation)" = "#1e88e5")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Seasonal AETI (mm)", fill = NULL, title = "Where the consumed water came from") +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: callout-warning
## Comparing crops

Citrus is an evergreen tree crop measured over a full year; wheat is
an annual crop measured over seven winter months. Their water
productivity values are **not a ranking** of which crop is more
efficient: season length, climate and the product (fresh fruit versus
dry grain) all differ. Compare each crop with its own benchmarks and
between farms of the same crop.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Glossary {.unnumbered}

| Term | Meaning |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| **Adequacy** | AETI divided by ETc. Below 1: the crop consumed less than its demand. |
| **AETI** | Actual EvapoTranspiration and Interception: all water leaving the land surface as vapour. |
| **AOI** | Area of interest: the outline of the study area. |
| **Beneficial fraction (BF)** | T divided by AETI: the share of consumption used by the crop. |
| **Biomass (DMP)** | Dry matter produced by the crop, from NPP. |
| **Blue water** | Consumption supplied by irrigation (or groundwater). |
| **BWP** | Biomass water productivity: dry biomass per m³ of water consumed. |
| **Crop mask** | Raster that marks which pixels belong to the crop being studied. |
| **CWP** | Crop water productivity: harvested yield per m³ of water consumed. |
| **Dekad** | A period of about 10 days: days 1 to 10, 11 to 20, and 21 to the end of each month. |
| **Effective rain (Peff)** | Part of the rain that stays in the root zone and can be used by the crop. |
| **ETc** | Crop evapotranspiration: water demand of a healthy, well-watered crop, $K_c \times RET$. |
| **Green water** | Consumption supplied by rain. |
| **Harvest index (HI)** | Harvested share of the above-ground biomass. |
| **Uniformity** | Evenness of water use within a field or block: 1 minus the CV of seasonal AETI of its pixels. |
| **Equity** | Evenness of water use between fields or blocks: CV of their mean seasonal AETI. |
| **Climate normalization factor** | Mean seasonal RET of the area divided by the RET of a field; removes the effect of weather when comparing fields. |
| **Kc** | Crop coefficient: ratio between the crop's demand and the reference ET, changing with growth stage. |
| **L1, L2, L3** | WaPOR resolution levels: about 300 m, 100 m and 20 m. |
| **NPP** | Net Primary Production: carbon fixed by the vegetation. |
| **P95** | The 95th percentile: the value exceeded by only the best 5% of pixels. |
| **RET** | Reference evapotranspiration: water demand of a reference grass surface, set by the weather. |
| **T** | Transpiration: water that passes through the plants. |
